name: Pope Francis
role: Head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of Vatican City (2013-2025)
summary: Francis taught a social doctrine that combined traditional Catholic positions on life, marriage and the priesthood with sharp criticism of unregulated markets, consumerism and nationalism. He urged welcome for migrants, cancellation of poor countries' debts, abolition of the death penalty and nuclear weapons, and drastic climate action, while rejecting abortion, euthanasia and same-sex marriage.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Urged government and financial leaders to ensure that all citizens have dignified work, education and healthcare, and lamented the dismantling of healthcare systems; he did not describe a specific state-run scheme.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Rejected trickle-down claims and the absolute autonomy of markets and financial speculation, and said the marketplace cannot resolve every problem.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Denounced worldwide tax evasion in Evangelii gaudium; a 2024 report cited by Wikipedia says he renewed calls for higher taxes on billionaires.

unions-good.rationale: Told Italian union leaders there is no good society without a good union, which gives a voice to those who have none.

property-fundamental.rationale: Wrote that the Christian tradition has never recognized private property as absolute or inviolable; it is a secondary right subordinate to the universal destination of goods.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Criticized ideologies that deny states any control over markets and called for oversight and enforcement of rules on business and technology in the common good.

cut-welfare.rationale: Said welfare projects are only temporary responses and that structural causes of poverty must be tackled; he never argued for cutting aid and rejected remedies that add to the ranks of the excluded.

worker-ownership.rationale: Praised workers united in cooperatives and recuperated businesses as creating work where there was none; this is approval of the model rather than a call for all workers to own their firms.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Told the 2014 International Drug Enforcement Conference that attempts to legalize recreational drugs are highly questionable and that drug use is not solved with drugs.

state-harmful.rationale: Held that states are charged with vigilance for the common good and criticized ideologies that deny states any role of control.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Condemning prostitution as a violation of dignity is a moral judgement, not a stated position on its legality.

decide-locally.rationale: Endorsed the principle of subsidiarity, under which lower-level communities participate and act, though he also asked for stronger international institutions.

rehabilitation.rationale: Said society can only benefit from the rehabilitation of those convicted of crimes and cited the death penalty as eliminating all hope of rehabilitation.

traditional-family.rationale: Wrote that weakening the family founded on marriage threatens society and that only the exclusive, indissoluble union of a man and a woman has a plenary social role.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Endorsed the Synod's finding that there are no grounds for likening same-sex unions to marriage and rejected pressure to legalize them.

abortion-legal.rationale: Called defence of unborn life non-negotiable, and wrote that concern for nature is incompatible with justifying abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Argued that healthy pluralism does not mean privatizing religion or confining it to individual conscience.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Apologies for wrongs to native peoples are nearby; no stated position on correcting historical racial injustice in society.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Denounced an ideology of gender that treats identity as individual choice detached from biological sexual difference.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Wrote that openness to others requires love for one's own land, people and cultural roots, while also warning against closed nationalism.

gradual-change.rationale: Preferred initiating processes over occupying spaces, but also said 'we want change, real change, structural change'.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Urged all countries to generous openness toward migrants and set out welcome, protect, promote and integrate as the response.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Called for stronger international institutions able to impose sanctions and a reform giving the UN real teeth.

free-trade.rationale: Criticism of particular trade treaties is nearby; no stated position on free trade in general.

nation-first.rationale: Criticized narrow nationalism and national interests placed above the global common good in climate negotiations.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Warned that wars are justified by allegedly humanitarian excuses but accepted the Catechism's legitimate defence under rigorous conditions.

open-borders.rationale: Said borders must not stand in the way of dignified opportunity and that each country belongs also to the foreigner in need, yet also that unnecessary migration should be avoided and states have a role.

limit-growth.rationale: Wrote that the time has come to accept decreased growth in some parts of the world and to contain growth by setting limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Called for a drastic, intense and binding energy transition and said the climate crisis is nearing a breaking point.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Wrote that seeking only a technical remedy to each environmental problem masks the deeper problems, and that supposing all problems will be solved by technology is mistaken.

basic-income.rationale: In an Easter 2020 letter said it might be the time to consider a universal basic wage for informal workers; later reports say he renewed the call in 2024.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Favouring smallholders is nearby; no stated general position on spreading property among small owners.

democracy-best.rationale: Described the American democratic tradition approvingly in Congress but warned that words like democracy can be bent into tools of domination.

war-builds-character.rationale: Said war is the negation of all rights and cannot any longer be thought of as a solution.

separate-church-state.rationale: Rejected relegating religion to the private sphere, while not asking for a union of church and state.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Called for the right of original peoples to their land, self-determination and prior consent, and said indigenous peoples care best for the land they remain on.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Wrote that other creatures have a value of their own and that species have value in themselves.

limit-population.rationale: Criticized proposals to reduce birth rates as a way of avoiding the problems of the poor and rejected aid conditioned on reproductive policies.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Criticized the technocratic paradigm and consumerism yet said it is right to rejoice in advances in technology and medicine.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Criticized a technocratic paradigm in which AI and innovations assume human limitlessness, and the speed of change relative to the common good.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Wrote that realities are greater than ideas and warned against ideas detached from reality; he also warned of technocratic efficiency.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The universal destination of goods is nearby; no stated position on distribution by need.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Spoke of the rights of peoples, including self-determination, alongside personal rights, and said person and people are correlative.

positive-liberty.rationale: Called claims to economic freedom while real conditions bar many from access to it doublespeak.

universal-morality.rationale: Taught that human dignity and rights rest on a truth about the person that holds in every situation and culture.

single-common-good.rationale: Criticized views of society as a sum of coexisting interests and called for politics oriented to the common good.

national-self-determination.rationale: Said no established power has the right to deprive peoples of the full exercise of their sovereignty and cited the right of peoples to independence.

force-without-un.rationale: Warned against preventive or unilateral wars on invented grounds and called for the UN's rule of law to be uncontested.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Rejected scientism and positivism, holding that knowledge includes philosophy, theology and faith itself, which seeks and trusts reason.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Listed guaranteed personal security, access to basic services, employment and a minimum to survive among measures owed to arriving migrants.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Criticized patriarchal cultures and women's lack of equal access to decision-making roles, while describing motherhood as a particular expression of women's care.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Said technology based on coal, oil and gas must be progressively replaced without delay.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Described the aim as integration while preserving each community's cultural and religious identity and open to differences.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Wrote that history is burdened by patriarchal excesses, that women lack equal access to dignified work and decision-making, and a declaration he approved says society does not yet reflect women's equal dignity.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Denounced corruption and worldwide tax evasion and said corruption discredits politics, yet called politics a noble form of charity.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Held that every human being has inalienable dignity and that all are brothers and sisters regardless of birth or origin.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Same affirmation of freedom to choose and manifest one's religion publicly; he asked Muslim countries to grant Christians freedom to worship.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Made the preferential option for the poor central to his teaching and called for the structural causes of poverty to be addressed first.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Said blaming population growth rather than extreme consumerism of some is a way of refusing to face the issues.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Held that a living culture enriched by others and a people open to welcoming differences grows stronger; he framed closed groups as the problem.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: A call for full citizenship rights is nearby; no stated position on residency periods.

death-penalty.rationale: Ordered the Catechism rewritten in 2018 to call the death penalty inadmissible and committed the Church to its worldwide abolition.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Supported age-appropriate sex education within an education for love with parents as primary educators, but denounced gender-related educational programmes as ideological colonization.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Appealed in the 2025 Jubilee bull for wealthy nations to forgive the debts of countries that can never repay them.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Asked affluent nations to forgive unpayable debts as a matter of justice and described an ecological debt owed by the global North to the South.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Said the possession of nuclear weapons is immoral and that peace cannot be built on the fear of mutual destruction.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Stated that private ownership is justified so goods can better serve the common good, and that the social function of property comes before private property.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Endorsed the precautionary principle, reversing the burden of proof where serious irreversible damage may result.

land-redistribution.rationale: Defending land access for the landless is nearby; no stated position on taking large estates.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Affirmed religious freedom as a fundamental right including the freedom to choose the religion one judges true.

no-bailouts.rationale: Criticized saving banks at any cost and making the public pay the price while foregoing a review of the whole system.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Quoted the Catechism that it is contrary to human dignity to cause animals to suffer or die needlessly.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Accepted human use and experimentation on animals within reasonable limits that contribute to saving human lives.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Taught that solidarity means restoring to the poor what belongs to them and that the wealthy hold goods for the benefit of all.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Called for a lifestyle free of the obsession with consumption and said less is more.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Said families have the right to an adequate family policy including fiscal measures, and lamented falling birth rates as selfishness; he rejected state-forced birth limitation.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Argued society needs marriage as an exclusive and indissoluble union and that weakening it harms society.

local-production.rationale: Favoured small-scale food production systems and warned that economies of scale force smallholders off their land.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Criticized the neoliberal market dogma and also warned that leftist ideologies tied to individualistic methods leave most people dependent on others' goodwill.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Wrote that the Shoah must not be forgotten and called it the enduring symbol of the depths of human evil.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: In a 2023 interview described laws criminalizing homosexuality as unjust and asked bishops to reverse support for them.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Said solidarity and subsidiarity allow the common good in a full and participatory democracy and praised popular movements as protagonists.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Said transgender people must be accepted and integrated, but a declaration he approved criticizes gender theory and sex change.

assisted-dying.rationale: Said the Church firmly opposes euthanasia and assisted suicide and affirmed conscientious objection for healthcare workers.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Told Christians to embrace Muslim immigrants with affection and respect and said authentic Islam opposes every form of violence.

social-market-economy.rationale: Called for a proactive economic policy favouring productive diversity and business creativity while rejecting market autonomy; he called business a noble vocation.

rich-first.rationale: Called the claim that growth encouraged by a free market will inevitably bring justice an opinion never confirmed by the facts.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Denounced austerity measures imposed through loan agencies as tightening the belt of workers and the poor and restricting countries' sovereignty.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Warned that an economy of exclusion and inequality kills, called inequality the root of social ills, and spoke of a new tyranny of unregulated markets.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Valued local communities and civil society (subsidiarity) but argued charity needs the institutions of an organized society and states must act for the common good.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Warning that ecological crisis threatens humanity is nearby; no stated position on extinction risk as a policy priority.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Said the reservation of the priesthood to men is not open to discussion, and in 2023-24 interviews said holy orders are reserved for men.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Rejected every form of sexual submission and read Paul's text on wives as mutual subjection.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Called the 1915 massacre of Armenians the first genocide of the 20th century, in 2015 and again in 2016.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Cited the Catechism on legitimate defence by military force under rigorous conditions, so he did not hold that defensive killing is always wrong.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: A declaration he approved calls sexual difference foundational and rejects the self-determination claimed by gender theory.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Criticized the tendency to privatize water and turn it into a market commodity, and said access to safe water is a universal human right; he named no other services.

person-over-state.rationale: Said politics must serve the human person and that a person is an end and never a means.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Taught that human beings have a spiritual dimension and that an ecological culture needs a spirituality.

gm-crops.rationale: Said no general judgement on genetic modification is possible, noting no conclusive proof of harm to humans but significant problems with concentrated ownership.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Rejected preventive attacks and precautionary excuses and recognized only legitimate defence under rigorous conditions.

future-generations.rationale: Said sustainable development cannot be spoken of apart from intergenerational solidarity and the common good extends to later generations.

arms-reduction.rationale: Called for integral disarmament and for confronting and stopping the arms trade.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Called for reform of international economic and financial institutions and for greater equity and a real share in decision-making for all countries.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Said the environment cannot be safeguarded by financial cost-benefit calculation or market forces and criticized carbon credits.

shared-human-nature.rationale: A declaration he approved grounds inalienable dignity and rights in a shared human nature rather than in cultural construction.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Called the possession of atomic weapons immoral and said deterrence does not protect against present threats.

women-suffrage.rationale: Called for women's rights and participation in public life to be promoted and for their presence where important decisions are made.

simple-living.rationale: Proposed a prophetic and contemplative lifestyle capable of deep enjoyment without consumption, and sober lifestyles in rich societies.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Condemned extrajudicial executions as homicides committed by states and their agents.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Teaching that resources serve all peoples is nearby; no stated position on compensation for appropriation.

notes: Died 21 April 2025, so treated as a historical figure; no answer is inferred, all rest on his own writings, speeches and acts, or on documents he approved. Dignitas infinita and Fiducia supplicans were issued by the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith with his approval and are used only at medium confidence or below. His tone on LGBT people softened (accompaniment, non-liturgical blessings, calling criminalization unjust) without changing the stated teaching on marriage.
